translation_notes: context shim: infixowl_shim.py carries classOrIdentifier verbatim (rdflib/extras/infixowl.py lines 237-243 of MKLab-ITI/prophet@eee2ab51de) plus the two marker classes its isinstance test needs. The vendored module itself cannot be imported: it is a python-2 era rdflib copy (from rdflib import py3compat) and the modern rdflib.extras.infixowl is a different, rewritten module.
original.py needed one added import line (from rdflib import Namespace): the extracted region carried the OWL_NS = Namespace(...) context line but not the import it needs

OWL_NS = Namespace("http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#") becomes @prefix owl: <...> . - the textbook mapping; nothing else in the region uses OWL_NS as a runtime object, so the Python binding disappears cleanly

self.graph.add((self.identifier, OWL_NS.complementOf, classOrIdentifier(other))) becomes self.graph += g{ {self.identifier} owl:complementOf {classOrIdentifier(other)} }; both subject and object are computed by Python code and are interpolated, so only the predicate really gains from the notation - a fair picture of what island syntax buys in library code, where terms come from the caller
driver covers all four paths: other as a URIRef, other as an infixowl Class (classOrIdentifier unwraps it), a blank-node subject, and the falsy-other early return
